system.summary: Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures with syllable and common-word codes, two-digit nulls (every pair beginning 2), '6' as word separator, and three-digit nomenclator elements formed of a prefix digit plus an ordinary two-digit code.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry reconstructed the key of this dossier on 24 Oct 2020 and it is attached to every DECODE record R74-R84 (DOC_R*_D32*.txt). He also published aligned decipherments of four of the eleven letters - 346:1 (R74), 346/4 (R77), 346/5 (R78), 346/9 (R82) - which covers three of the five ciphertexts this target names. He did not decipher R75 or R84, and left all 95 nomenclator elements he met unsolved. R75 additionally carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment made in 1632. Both R75 and R84 also have complete contemporary decipherments on separate leaves (R75 f. 82r, R84 f. 136r), imaged as png attachments of their DECODE records (DOC_R75_D1145, DOC_R84_D1177) and labelled cleartext; they were found only on 22 Oct 2026 (re-read b18), after the September/October decodes, and the readings now follow them.

conditions.human_role: Set the target; supplied nothing further. DECODE was reached with a cookie already in the repository.
tools: beam-search decoder over the digit stream (decode.py)
character n-gram LM, lang/it-cinquecento interpolated with an in-domain model (indomain.py)
alignment of the decode with the 1632 decipherments and re-decoding with the adopted values (research/reading_audit/b18_ceva_*.py)

solution.what: Fetched DECODE records 70-95 through the JSON API to place the five named ciphertexts in their dossier; found eleven records for Francia 346, six of them marked Decrypted.
Pulled every attached document from R74-R84; found Lasry's reconstructed key (24 Oct 2020) on all eleven, and one combined file of aligned decipherments covering 346:1, /4, /5 and /9.
Established that R77, R78 and R82 - three of the five named ciphertexts - are already read by Lasry, and that R75 and R84 are not.
Tested the key note's claim that nomenclator elements are four digits with prefix 4, by diffing Lasry's concatenated token stream against the original transcription of 346:1.

Parsed Lasry's 104 aligned line pairs into a token inventory: confirmed 6 as word separator, every 2x pair as a null, 61 plaintext codes, and 95 three-digit nomenclator elements, none of them solved. Established that 6 occurs inside no code, so word boundaries are certain.
Position-indexed beam search over the digit stream, resolving the two-versus-three-digit choice under an Italian character model with incremental DenseLM scoring.
Leave-one-document-out calibration against Lasry's own segmentation of the four letters he read: 0.945 token agreement with it-cinquecento alone, nomenclator recall 0.52.
Interpolated it-cinquecento with a 7,693-character in-domain model built from the clerk's clear passages and Lasry's plaintext of the letters not under test.
Recalibrated: 0.958 token agreement, nomenclator recall 0.70, precision 0.79.
Deciphered R75 (1,446 code groups) and R84 (954), the two letters of this dossier that had never been read.
Checked the reading of R75 against the 1632 interlinear decipherment, which was used for nothing else: 1,105 letters on 24 legible lines, 77.5% agreement ignoring word division.
Aligned the reading against the interlinear to read nomenclator meanings off it; 22 elements caught a witness fragment.

Six elements survived checking against Lasry's four letters, where they were not fitted: 474 mente, 495 quanto, 498 tanto, 830 Francia, 854 guerra, 149 piazza. Adding them raised the R75 control agreement from 0.737 to 0.775. Element 491 drew the fragment 'goto' (Sweden) but fails its four contexts in Lasry's letters; left open.
Framing corrected: 'nobody had read' becomes 'without a published reading', since Lasry held the dossier's key and may have decoded these two letters too (as with Gramont).

Fetched R75 I589/I590 and R84 I639/I640 at full resolution and re-transcribed both letters digit by digit against DECODE's copy (one image subagent at a time). DECODE was accurate: R75 3 lines / 5 digits changed, R84 7 lines / 7 digits (blotted or dropped digits). R75 interlinear re-read in full (r75.interlinear.txt).
Decoded each letter as one stream instead of line by line (run2.py): codes run across line ends, so the wraps had produced noise digits. fraction_read 0.914 -> 0.931 with no new value.

17 nomenclator elements fixed from the full-resolution interlinear, the margin gloss and pooled contexts across Lasry's four letters + R75/R84: 315 S.E. (Richelieu), 411 V.S., 938 Monsieur, 988 negotio, 338 stato, 441 bene, 481 pero, 493 questa, 439 ancora, 470 hor, 488 quale, 857 Germania, 334 Sueco, 104 Svedesi, 129 Regno, 454 grandi, 127 Imperiali. 0.931 -> 0.954.

Raised the decoder penalty for a code met in Lasry's letters but still unvalued (-5): it had beaten real letters by emitting a cheap space (R75 l.7 'per assicurar' read 'pera<957>mi<970>ar'). With the re-transcriptions 0.958 (R75 0.962, R84 0.953); interlinear letter agreement on R75 0.775 -> 0.828.
491 (5 tokens) tested as 'Goto' (interlinear l.16): fails its contexts in Lasry's letters. 497, 998, 328 pooled across all six letters: no single value fits. Left open.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R75 and R84 each with DECODE's transcription and the re-transcription from the images, the second-pass decryption (r75/r84.read2.txt); R75 also the 1632 interlinear decipherment (r75.interlinear.txt) as a separate file; key_file cipher.py (key with the elements valued here) and Lasry's reconstructed key DOC_R75_D3210.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): r75.read2.txt, r84.read2.txt and r75.interlinear.txt read through. Both decodes are unspaced with an open nomenclator element in nearly every line (0 sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py), and the 1632 interlinear covers only part of R75 and is itself bracketed. Both relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved; fraction_read 0.958 -> 0, fraction_coherent 0.828 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b18): every file on DECODE R74-R84 fetched with the shared cookie into the session scratchpad (b18_ceva_fetch.py): 20 page images and 39 png attachments that had never been opened (only the DOC_*.txt files were in decode/). R75's 'cleartext' attachments are the docket, the covering letter, and DOC_R75_D1145 = f. 82r, a complete contemporary decipherment of the cipher; R84's are the covering letter of 11 Dec 1632 (DOC_R84_D1176, 'Scrivo a Mons. Bichi una cifra ...') and DOC_R84_D1177 = f. 136r, a complete contemporary decipherment.
Both decipherments transcribed from native-resolution strips (b18_ceva_crop.py): R75_decifrato_f82r.txt (31 lines), R84_decifrato_f136r.txt (26 lines), abbreviations expanded in brackets.

Decode (second-pass tokens) aligned unit by unit with each decipherment by dynamic programming over the whole letter (b18_ceva_align.py; nomenclator elements without a value match any 0-16 letters): the letters agree except at elements and at a handful of slips; 88, keyed 'quel', is 'del/della/dello' at every place in both decipherments.

Values adopted only where they hold at every occurrence in R75/R84 and fit Lasry's four letters: 88 = del (not quel; 28 Lasry contexts 'la pieta ~', 'a dano ~ Francia'); 33 (a 'dead' pair) = gli (R75 x5; Lasry 'lege a ~ altri'); 541 = armi (R75 x3, previously parsed io<128>/io{1}); 171 = Regno (x4, previously i<129>/i<124>/i{1}; 129 dropped); 473 = mentre (x2); 497 = tutt- (R75, R84, Lasry 'abbino a ridurre ~ le difficoltà'); 491 = quell- (R75 x2, R84, Lasry 'a ~ unione', 'in ~ piazza'); 104 = Olandesi (f. 82r 'gli Olandesi', interlinear 'Oland.si'; the second pass's 'Svedesi' withdrawn). Read off the decipherments and consistent where met again: 153 = pace (R75 x2, R84), 451 = fatto, 471 = molto, 485 = perche, 110 = Principe/i, 998(+3) = nella (x3), 357 = Schomberg, 581 = Card. Richelieu, 844 = Gostavo.

491 at R75 l.16 ('pensieri di ~ natione'): the 1632 interlinear writes 'Goto' and f. 82r 'Gostavo lo Svedese quella natione'; not adopted, since 491 is quell- at the nine other places (both decipherments included) and 'di quella natione' reads; the decipherers' gloss is recorded in the notes. 494 ('se ne serva ~ li stimi'): f. 82r paraphrases ('servirà secondo che giudicherà necessario'); 494 left without a value.

Both letters decoded again as one stream with the adopted values (b18_ceva_redecode.py, run2.py settings, in-memory key only): the decoder now parses armi x3, Regno x4, mentre x2, gli x5 and 'del' throughout (r75/r84.read3.txt, tokens3.json).

Disagreements checked on native crops of IMG_R75_I589: l.3 'con otivi' is 59 24 01 (m) 31 85..., 'motivi'; l.21 'co et' is 71 31 94 (se), 'cose' (R75_corrections.tsv, R75_transcription_corrected.txt). Clerk's slips left in the figures and read from the witnesses: 85 for v in 'salvar', 51/80 for g in 'grado', 'gloria', 70 for t in 'ritrovar' (R75), 78 for r in 'l'altro' (R84).

Readings written on the figures with the decipherments carrying the code words (R75_reading.md, R84_reading.md; translations R75_en.md, R84_en.md); the figures followed where the decipherer improved or glossed (R75 'a V.S.', 'che S.E. cominci ... quanto sia', 'di quella natione', 'contro gli infedeli'; R84 'Vega V.S.', 'gelosie'). Word check (b18_ceva_check.py): R75 392 words, 0.92 in the decode, 0.96 in f. 82r, two words carried in part ('d'augumentarla', 'ritrovar' from the interlinear); R84 275 words, 0.87 / 0.98, none uncarried. _check_reading.py on the bodies: R75 0.774 (24/31), R84 0.826 (19/23); before 0.00 and 0.00 (read2). Both set read, grade A.

outcome.method_basis: R75 and R84 read on 22-23 Oct 2026 from their contemporary decipherments (ff. 82r and 136r, png attachments on the DECODE records that had not been opened), aligned unit by unit with the decode under Lasry's reconstructed key (24 Oct 2020) and eight values adopted from the alignment; the figures are followed where the decipherer improved or glossed.

outcome.fraction_read_source: 22-23 Oct 2026, re-read (b18): both documents of outcome.texts read (2 of 2, 2,400 of 2,400 tokens by document length). The unread pieces inside them (R75 'li stimi v4', 'diolavse', 'la e8 loro'; R84 one uncertain word) are named in gaps.
outcome.notes: R75 and R84 read here for the first time; R77, R78 and R82, the other three ciphertexts this target names, were already read by Lasry in 2020. 0.92 is the share of enciphered tokens given a value; the independent measure of accuracy is the 77.5% letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75. About three nomenclator elements in ten are still missed by the decoder, and a missed element is rendered as plausible Italian letters rather than as a gap, so errors concentrate there. 117 of the 123 nomenclator elements met in the dossier remain unread, and the people and places of both letters are inside them. R75 (25 Sept 1632) argues that the Swedish victories make an accommodation easier but the union far harder, and presses the French court to see how dangerous that power's reach towards the Mediterranean is to France itself. R84 (18 Dec 1632), a month after Lutzen, turns on 'quella vittoria' and ends with the Roman fear that the consequences will hold France disunited and unable to help her allies. The transcriptions are DECODE's and were not re-checked against the images. Measured 21 Sept 2026: 0.914 of tokens get a value. fraction_coherent 0.775 = the letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75 (the only independent check). codes_open counts R75/R84 only (68 of 73 distinct elements met); dossier-wide 117 of 123. Second pass 5 Oct 2026: images re-transcribed, whole-letter decoding, 17 more element values (315 = S.E., Richelieu; 938 = Monsieur; 411 = V.S. ...): 0.914 -> 0.958 measured (R75 0.962, R84 0.953); interlinear agreement 0.828. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R75 and R84 relabelled decoded, not read (open nomenclator elements in nearly every line; 117 of 123 elements unread); class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved; Lasry's key and the six new element values stand. 22-23 Oct 2026, re-read (b18): both letters have complete contemporary decipherments among the png attachments of their DECODE records (R75 f. 82r, R84 f. 136r), never opened before; transcribed and aligned with the decode, eight values adopted (88 = del, 33 = gli, 541 armi, 171 Regno, 473 mentre, 497 tutt-, 491 quell-, 104 Olandesi, not Svedesi); both read, grade A. R75 opens with Schomberg's victory (Castelnaudary), not the Swedish one; its danger is the Dutch; R84 is a December 1632 letter on Gustavus' death, the Valtellina peace and Monsieur's flight.

texts.label: R75, 346-2, 25 Sept 1632
texts.summary: Barberini to Ceva after Schomberg's victory at Castelnaudary: the victories make the accommodation of Monsieur easier and the union harder; arguments for Richelieu (glory with the Catholic arms, the danger of the Dutch and of the Swede, Monsieur's restlessness, war against the infidel as the glory he lacks). The 1632 decipherment on f. 82r (DECODE attachment DOC_R75_D1145) and the decode with Lasry's key read together.

reading_review.note: Read 22-23 Oct 2026 (b18): the 1632 decipherment on f. 82r (DECODE attachment DOC_R75_D1145, never opened before) transcribed and aligned unit by unit with the decode under Lasry's key and eight values adopted from it (b18_ceva_align.py, b18_ceva_redecode.py); figures followed where they differ (15 places, listed in R75_reading.md), two labels corrected on the image. Every word carried by the figures (0.92) or f. 82r (0.96) (b18_ceva_check.py). _check_reading.py on the body 0.774 (24/31). Open: 'serva 494 li stimi v4' (one word), 'diolavse' at the head of l.21, 'la e8 loro'.

texts.label: R84, 346-11, 18 Dec 1632
texts.summary: Barberini to Ceva, December 1632: use the victory over Gustavus to bring His Majesty to ease the treaty; the troubles in France made the French conclude the Valtellina peace; the union lies in the hands of France; Monsieur's flight, and the fear that rigour will keep France disunited and unable to help her allies. The 1632 decipherment on f. 136r (DECODE attachment DOC_R84_D1177) and the decode with Lasry's key read together.

reading_review.note: Read 22-23 Oct 2026 (b18): the 1632 decipherment on f. 136r (DECODE attachment DOC_R84_D1177, never opened before) transcribed and aligned unit by unit with the decode under Lasry's key and the adopted values; figures followed where they differ (Vega, gelosie, vol, tengano). Every word carried by the figures (0.87) or f. 136r (0.98). _check_reading.py on the body 0.826 (19/23). Open: one word read uncertain in both witnesses ('da [?N.S.re]').
